entries.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
entries.summary: Three drawn positions of a dumbbell Romanian deadlift, seen from the side.

provenance.positions: Authored for this repository from its own curated execution instructions and coaching cues for movement_id 88 (packages/core-db/src/schema/017_movement_batch.sql, 025_movement_coaching_content.sql).
instructionAgreement: stand — "Stand with dumbbells resting on the front of your thighs."
hinge — "Push your hips straight back and let the dumbbells slide down your legs, knees softly bent"; the hips travel back while the knees stay softly bent.

bottom — dumbbells drawn at mid-shin with a flat back, the depth the instructions describe as "until the hamstrings tell you to stop"; the load stays against the legs, per "daylight between them and you means the load has wandered onto your back".
provenance.artwork: No third-party artwork. Every frame is a list of joint coordinates in this file, drawn at runtime from plain React Native views.
provenance.licence: Original work created for this repository; covered by the repository licence.

entries.reviewNotes: Side view only. Bottom depth varies with hamstring length; the drawn depth is one common range, not a target. No qualified technique reviewer has signed this off yet.
entries.limitations: Three frames cannot show the moment the back starts rounding, which is the real stopping signal in the instructions.

frames.caption: Stand tall with the dumbbells resting on the front of the thighs
Push the hips back; the dumbbells slide down to the knees, knees softly bent
Dumbbells at mid-shin, back flat and long, hamstrings loaded

frames.caption: Stand tall with the bar close to the thighs and a soft bend in the knees.
Send the hips back while the bar tracks down the legs.
The bar tracks down the legs until the hamstrings are loaded.
Drive the hips through to stand, keeping the bar close.
Stand tall through the hips with the trunk still long.

entries.name: Cable Deadlifts
entries.summary: Seven drawn positions of a cable deadlift, seen from the side.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository after owner review: a neutral upright start between the two low stacks (ruling 4), hips travelling on the exact thigh circle and the torso rotating on the exact spine so knees extend with the hips on the drive, arms long to the handles throughout, and the near cable running to a low pulley just ahead of the toes. The pulley position and the knee coupling are listed as open questions for the owner at the checkpoint. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

frames.caption: Stand tall between the stacks, a handle in each hand, cables just off the stack.
Brace before the cables leave the stack.
Sit the hips back and take the handles with long arms.
Handles near the shins; the hamstrings carry the load.
Push the floor away; extend the hips and knees together.
Handles finish beside the thighs, tall and braced.
Stand tall again; ready for the next rep.

entries.name: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: the bar is carried across the shoulders in the rack position, drawn end-on with its plates, while the hips travel on the exact thigh circle and the torso rotates on the exact spine with the neck constant. The bar, elbows and hands ride rigidly with the torso, so every drawn length is constant. No media row exists in the database under this name; the standard rack-position setup was drawn (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a stiff leg barbell good morning, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Stand tall with the bar across your shoulders, clear of the neck.
Set the ribs down and brace first.
Send the hips back into the load.
Posterior chain loaded; keep the back quiet.
Drive the hips through and stand.
Finish tall through the glutes.

frames.caption: Hike the bell close between the legs with a long flat back.
Snap the hips to stand tall and let the bell rise.
The bell leaves the legs behind as the hips finish.
Arms stay long while the bell swings up.
The bell floats at chest height with quiet, long arms.
Guide the bell back down as the hips reload.
The bell returns along the same arc.
The hinge reloads to meet the bell.
Hike the bell back between the legs for the next rep.

entries.name: Band Good Morning
techniqueCitations: Video: Band Good Morning technique demonstration (YouTube, video ID CTRaCzE8pWU).
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: a side-view hip hinge with a long band under the mid-foot and across the back of the shoulders, held at the front with elbows soft. The band runs behind the knee and up the back; it visibly stretches through the drive. The hips travel on the exact thigh circle and the torso rotates on the exact spine, with the neck constant, so every drawn bone keeps its length. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a band good morning, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Stand tall with the band across your shoulders, clear of the neck.
Brace first, then send the hips back.
Hinge until the hamstrings load; keep the band over mid-foot.
Drive the floor away and squeeze the glutes.
Finish tall through the glutes.

entries.name: Power Clean
entries.reason: An Olympic-derived lift. Pull, triple extension, turnover and catch cannot be depicted honestly in about three frames, and a coarse drawing of a fast lift invites imitation of the wrong shape.
